title: Comparison of AlphaFold3 Folding and DNA Binding Predictions for the C-Terminal Domain of Topoisomerase II&#945; and II&#946;
content: Topoisomerases are a family of enzymes that relieve torsional strain in DNA. Type II topoisomerases utilize a temporary, enzyme-bound double-stranded break to relax, decatenate, or unknot DNA segments. Anticancer agents can disrupt topoisomerase II function and lead cell death, but there is a risk of off target toxicity including secondary leukemia or cardiotoxicity. Humans have two isoforms: topoisomerase IIa (TOP2A) and topoisomerase IIb (TOP2B), and current therapeutics cannot distinguish between these enzymes. We are interested in targeting TOP2A, which is more involved in replication and mitosis, and we hypothesize that avoiding TOP2B may reduce off-target toxicity. Both isoforms share much of their sequence and structure, but they also have intrinsically disordered C-terminal domains (CTD) that are very different in terms of primary structure. We hypothesized that new therapeutics could be designed to target this region of the enzyme. Therefore, we employed AlphaFold3 (AF3) to explore the possible folding conformations of the CTD of TOP2B similar to our previous study of TOP2A. AF3 predicts folding of TOP2B CTD when post-translational modifications and DNA are added to the structure prediction. We find that with both TOP2A and TOP2B, AF3 predicts increased helical structure within the CTD upon the addition of DNA to the model. We explored the AF3 predictions and utilized Edison Scientific to analyze the AF3 outputs. We identified regions within TOP2A that do not align with TOP2B and also are predicted to change secondary structure in the presence of DNA. We hypothesize that these regions may be of interest to explore for impact on TOP2A function with the potential for developing future therapeutics.
